prompt: A server goes from 16.2 to 16.15. What happens to the files in its data directory?
hint: A minor release never changes the on-disk format.

choices.text: pg_upgrade rewrites the catalogue
choices.why: That is a major upgrade. Between minor releases the catalogue does not change.

choices.text: They are converted on first access
choices.why: PostgreSQL never converts files lazily. There is nothing to convert between minor releases.

choices.text: Nothing; the new programs open the same files after a restart
choices.why: Right. 16.15 reads exactly what 16.2 wrote; only the programs and a restart change.

choices.text: They must be dumped and restored
choices.why: A dump is one way across a major version. A minor upgrade needs none.

prompt: A server runs 16.2. Which path to 16.15 does the lesson describe?
hint: Minor releases are cumulative.

choices.text: Install each release from 16.3 to 16.15 in turn, restarting after each one
choices.why: Each minor release contains every fix before it, so the ones in between add nothing.

choices.text: Straight to 16.15, reading each release's notes
choices.why: Right. 16.15 contains everything in 16.3 to 16.14. You still read the release notes of each.

choices.text: Upgrade to 17 first, then come back
choices.why: A major version cannot be undone by installing older programs; the data directory would be 17's.

choices.text: Through 16.10, the last release that changes the format
choices.why: No minor release changes the on-disk format, so there is no stepping stone.

prompt: Match each way across a major version to its way back if the new version misbehaves.
hint: Which ones leave the old cluster able to start?

pairs.right: Point the application back at the old server, still running

prompt: After `sudo apt install postgresql-16`, what showed that the server had really been restarted?
hint: Two values were asked before and after.

choices.text: `pg_postmaster_start_time()` returned a later time
choices.why: Right. The postmaster's start time moved, and the log shows the shutdown and the start between.

choices.text: apt printed a line saying the cluster was restarted
choices.why: The lesson quotes none of apt's output; the evidence came from the server itself.

choices.text: `pg_lsclusters` showed a new port
choices.why: The port stays 5432 through a minor upgrade.

choices.text: The data directory had a new name
choices.why: It is /var/lib/postgresql/16/main before and after; nothing in it changed.

prompt: The log shows `received fast shutdown request` during the upgrade. What does that mean for a client that was in the middle of a transaction?
hint: Fast is not smart.

choices.text: Rolled back, and disconnected
choices.why: Right. A fast shutdown rolls back open transactions and drops every connection; the client reconnects afterwards.

choices.text: The server waits for it to commit before stopping
choices.why: That would be a smart shutdown. A fast one does not wait for anybody.

choices.text: Its transaction is carried over into the 16.15 server
choices.why: No transaction survives a server restart; there is no process left to hold it.

choices.text: Nothing, because a minor upgrade does not stop the server
choices.why: It does stop it, for a few seconds, and the log shows exactly when.

prompt: A team finds their PostgreSQL restarted at 06:20 on a Tuesday with nobody logged in. `apt list --upgradable` had shown the new version in `noble-security` the day before. What is the likely cause?
hint: What installs security updates by itself on Ubuntu?

choices.text: unattended-upgrades installed the minor release
choices.why: Right. It installs packages from the security pocket daily, and the package's scripts restart the cluster.

choices.text: Autovacuum restarted it
choices.why: Autovacuum never restarts the server.

choices.text: The checkpointer did it
choices.why: A checkpoint writes dirty pages; it does not restart anything.

choices.text: The kernel's out-of-memory killer, which every security update triggers
choices.why: Security updates do not trigger the OOM killer, and the timing matches the update, not memory.

prompt: `sudo pg_createcluster 16 rehearsal --start` gave the new cluster port 5433. Why that port?
hint: What already holds 5432?

choices.text: Rehearsal clusters always use 5433
choices.why: The name means nothing to pg_createcluster; it only looks for a free port.

choices.text: 5433 is kept for a second version
choices.why: This cluster is 16, like main. No port is tied to a version.

choices.text: It was the next free port after main's 5432
choices.why: Right. main holds 5432, so pg_createcluster took the next free port.

choices.text: It copies main's port and adds one
choices.why: It writes a fresh configuration; the port is chosen by looking at what is taken.

prompt: Copying main into the rehearsal with `pg_dumpall | psql -p 5433` printed `ERROR: role "postgres" already exists`. What does that error mean for the copy?
hint: What does a fresh cluster already contain?

choices.text: Nothing; one statement failed and the rest ran
choices.why: Right. The new cluster already had a postgres role, so only that CREATE ROLE failed.

choices.text: The copy stopped there and must be repeated with --clean
choices.why: psql carries on after an error unless told to stop, and the count of orders showed the data arrived.

choices.text: Every role was skipped, so ana does not exist on 5433
choices.why: Only the one statement failed; the other roles were created.

choices.text: It now shares main's postgres role
choices.why: Each cluster has its own roles. Nothing is shared between clusters.

prompt: A colleague says the rehearsal is pointless because the rehearsal database is only a copy, and copies upgrade exactly like the original. Which reason from the lesson answers them best?
hint: Which problems are properties of the server rather than of the rows?

choices.text: A copy upgrades faster, so the rehearsal measures nothing
choices.why: If the copy has production's size, its times are production's times; that is a reason to rehearse.

choices.text: The rehearsal tests whether the data itself is corrupt
choices.why: pg_upgrade does not read the data files at all, so it would not notice corruption.

choices.text: It finds the failures cheaply
choices.why: Right. A missing extension build, a renamed setting or too little disk shows up on the copy, where a refusal costs nothing.

choices.text: Upgrading a copy upgrades the original too, through the shared files
choices.why: The rehearsal shares no files with main; it was filled by a dump.

prompt: What does `pg_upgradecluster 16 rehearsal` do when `-m upgrade` is left out?
hint: Its default method.

choices.text: pg_upgrade with --link
choices.why: Linking has to be asked for, and so does pg_upgrade.

choices.text: A dump and restore, its default method when none is given
choices.why: Right. dump is the default, correct but as slow as the data is big; -m upgrade chooses pg_upgrade.

choices.text: It refuses and asks for a method
choices.why: It has a default and uses it without asking.

choices.text: pg_upgrade copying the files
choices.why: That is -m upgrade without --link, which still needs -m upgrade.

prompt: The first `pg_upgradecluster` failed at `Checking for presence of required libraries`. In what state did it leave the old cluster?
hint: Where is that check relative to the line about re-initdb?

choices.text: Unusable, because --link had already linked its files
choices.why: Linking comes after every check; nothing had been linked when it failed.

choices.text: Stopped, waiting for the administrator to start it
choices.why: pg_upgradecluster printed `Starting old cluster again` and did so.

choices.text: Running again, as before
choices.why: Right. The checks run before any file is touched, so it dropped the new cluster and restarted the old one.

choices.text: Half upgraded, with its catalogue in 17's format
choices.why: The old catalogue is never rewritten; the new one is built in the new cluster.

prompt: After the --link upgrade, `ls -li` showed the orders table's file in both data directories. What link count did it show?
hint: One file, how many names?

prompt: After an upgrade with --link, somebody removes the `.old` suffix from `pg_control` and starts the 16 cluster to compare a query with 17. What happens to the data?
hint: Whose files are they now?

choices.text: 16 starts read-only
choices.why: There is no such mode; PostgreSQL has no idea another server owns the files.

choices.text: 16 and 17 corrupt the pages they share
choices.why: Right. The files are shared, 17 has already written into them, and 16 reads and writes the same pages.

choices.text: 16 refuses to start
choices.why: 16's own catalogue is still there in 16's format; the danger is the shared data files.

choices.text: Each cluster gets its own copy the first time it writes
choices.why: Hard links are not copy-on-write; a write through either name changes the one file.

prompt: To dump a 16 database for a 17 server, which pg_dump does the lesson use?
hint: The wrapper would have picked the other one.

choices.text: 16's, because the dump must match the server it reads
choices.why: A newer pg_dump reads older servers; it is the newer one that knows what 17 needs.

choices.text: Either; the dump format is the same in every version
choices.why: The lesson's advice is explicit: the new version's pg_dump. The reverse is not promised to work.

choices.text: pg_dumpall
choices.why: pg_dump crosses versions fine. pg_dumpall was used only for the roles.

choices.text: 17's, by its full path
choices.why: Right. /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin/pg_dump, because plain pg_dump ran 16's for the cluster on 5432.

prompt: `pg_dump shop` does not contain the role ana, because roles belong to the cluster. They come from `pg_dumpall --___-only`.
hint: Not schema, not data.

prompt: The restored orders indexes were 37 MB against 42 MB on main. Why?
hint: When was each index built, relative to the rows?

choices.text: 17 compresses indexes and 16 does not
choices.why: Neither compresses B-tree indexes; the difference is in how they were built.

choices.text: pg_dump left one of the indexes out
choices.why: Every CREATE INDEX was in the dump and the restore built each one.

choices.text: Autovacuum on main had not yet removed the dead rows in them
choices.why: shop was loaded once and never updated, so its indexes carry no dead rows.

choices.text: Built in one pass, after the data
choices.why: Right. shop.sql created the indexes before loading, so they grew by page splits; the restore built them packed.

prompt: Why was the publisher a third 16 cluster rather than main?
hint: What does wal_level need?

choices.text: Changing wal_level needs a restart
choices.why: Right. The lesson leaves main untouched, so the publisher was created with wal_level = logical already set.

choices.text: main has no primary keys
choices.why: Both tables of shop have primary keys.

choices.text: shop cannot hold a publication
choices.why: The publication was created in a database called shop.

choices.text: Logical replication works only between clusters created on the same day
choices.why: Nothing about logical replication depends on when a cluster was created.

prompt: Put the steps of the logical-replication upgrade in the order the lesson ran them.
hint: The tables must exist before anything can fill them.
items: Create a publication on the 16 server
Copy the schema alone into the 17 database
Wait until every table is in state r
Move every sequence past the largest id in use
trap: Fixing the sequences before the switch leaves them behind again as new rows arrive from the old server.

prompt: After the subscription was dropped, the first insert on 17 failed with `Key (id)=(1) already exists`. What had not been replicated?
hint: Rows arrived. What is not a row?

choices.text: The orders_pkey index
choices.why: The index exists; that is why the duplicate was caught.

choices.text: The sequence's position
choices.why: Right. orders_id_seq stood at 1 on the subscriber; setval moved it past the largest id.

choices.text: The rows inserted after the initial copy
choices.why: Order 1,000,001 arrived on 17 within a moment.

choices.text: The table's identity column definition, which pg_dump --schema-only leaves out
choices.why: The identity column was there; it handed out 1 because its sequence had never moved.

prompt: Which of these does pg_upgrade NOT carry into the new cluster?
hint: Its own output says so.

choices.text: The planner's statistics about each column's values
choices.why: Right. `Optimizer statistics are not transferred by pg_upgrade`; vacuumdb --analyze-in-stages makes them again.

choices.text: The roles and their passwords
choices.why: `Restoring global objects in the new cluster` carried them.

choices.text: The indexes
choices.why: Index files are linked or copied like table files.

choices.text: The extensions installed in each database
choices.why: They came across, at their old version, which is why update_extensions.sql exists.

prompt: `pg_dropcluster 16 rehearsal` deleted the old data directory, yet the orders on 17 were all still there. Why?
hint: How many names did each file have?

choices.text: pg_dropcluster copies shared files to the new cluster before deleting
choices.why: It copies nothing; it removes the directory, and the file survives through its other name.

choices.text: 17 had already rewritten every table into its own files
choices.why: 17 rewrote nothing; the inode was the same in both directories.

choices.text: Files in use are skipped
choices.why: It deleted the whole old directory; the data survived for another reason.

choices.text: The other name kept each file
choices.why: Right. A file is freed when its last link goes, and 17/rehearsal still held one.

prompt: After the upgrade, `pg_stat_statements` still said version 1.10 until `ALTER EXTENSION pg_stat_statements ___;` moved it to 1.11.
hint: One word, the same one update_extensions.sql used.

prompt: A 3 TB database must move to 17 with at most twenty minutes of downtime, and the disk has 1 TB free. Which method fits?
hint: Rule out by space first, then by time.

choices.text: pg_upgrade copying the files
choices.why: Copying needs room for a second 3 TB, and there is 1 TB.

choices.text: pg_upgrade --link, after a backup that is the way back
choices.why: Right. Linking needs almost no extra disk and takes about as long at any size; the backup is the way back.

choices.text: A dump and restore, which also removes the bloat
choices.why: Dumping and restoring 3 TB takes far longer than twenty minutes of stopped writes.

choices.text: A minor upgrade with apt
choices.why: apt cannot take 16 to 17; a major version needs one of the three methods.

prompt: On the night, `sudo pg_upgradecluster -m upgrade --link 16 main` stops at once with an error before touching anything. The package installed 17 a week ago. What is the first thing to check?
hint: What did installing the package create?

choices.text: Whether main has been analysed recently
choices.why: Statistics play no part in whether the upgrade starts; they are rebuilt afterwards.

choices.text: Whether wal_level is set to logical on main
choices.why: That matters for logical replication, not for pg_upgrade.

choices.text: Whether the minor release of 16 is the very latest one
choices.why: pg_upgrade does not demand the newest minor release; it compares major versions.

choices.text: Whether the package's empty 17/main is still there
choices.why: Right. The package created an empty 17/main, and pg_upgradecluster refuses a target cluster that exists; drop it after checking it is empty.

prompt: Match each message to what it is telling you.
hint: Each one appeared in this lesson.

pairs.left: database files are incompatible with server
pairs.right: A newer server was given an older major version's data directory

pairs.left: Checking for presence of required libraries ... fatal
pairs.right: An extension has no build for the new version
The old cluster was disabled after a --link upgrade

pairs.left: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "orders_pkey"
pairs.right: A sequence was not moved after logical replication

prompt: Which of these must still be done after a successful `pg_upgradecluster -m upgrade --link`? Choose all that apply.
hint: Some were done by the wrapper's analyze step.

choices.text: Run the ALTER EXTENSION ... UPDATE statements in update_extensions.sql
choices.why: Yes. Extensions keep their old version until updated.

choices.text: Test the application against the new cluster
choices.why: Yes. Nothing in the upgrade checks your application's queries.

choices.text: Rebuild any physical standby
choices.why: Yes. A standby cannot follow a primary of another major version.

choices.text: Run vacuumdb --all --analyze-in-stages by hand
choices.why: pg_upgradecluster's analyze step already ran it; last_analyze showed when.

choices.text: Run delete_old_cluster.sh to free the old data files
choices.why: On Ubuntu pg_dropcluster removes the old cluster, its configuration and its log, once the new one is checked.

prompt: A team wants to move from 16 on Ubuntu to 17 on a new ARM server, and change the cluster's locale while they are at it. Which method can do all of that?
hint: pg_upgrade needs both clusters on one machine with compatible settings.

choices.text: pg_upgrade --link
choices.why: Links only exist inside one filesystem, and pg_upgrade needs compatible settings on one machine.

choices.text: Dump and restore
choices.why: Right. A dump is SQL; it does not care about machine, architecture or locale.

choices.text: pg_upgrade copying the files to the new server over the network
choices.why: pg_upgrade copies within one machine, and the data files of one architecture are not readable on another.

choices.text: A minor upgrade first, which changes the locale
choices.why: A minor upgrade changes the programs and nothing else.
